knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun aa600f3fb29146a99e15abbec79139fd indices 18-20): the committed history the three rejecting nodes consumed in order is index 2 = ConfChangeV2 transition JointImplicit removing node 4 (change type 1, node 4) and index 4 = ConfChangeV2 transition JointImplicit adding node 4 (change type 0, node 4), with a normal entry at index 3 between them and no leave-joint entry anywhere in the range [firstIndex, committed]. So the log enters a joint configuration through a change that removes a node which is not a member of the voter set - a change that alters nothing about who votes - and then enters a second joint configuration from within the first, which is the entry each node's Changer rejects with 'config is already joint'.
knowledge.conditions: Sweep revision with four real raft instances, configuration targets drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, application lag skipping one node's apply about one time in six, restarts, default DisableConfChangeValidation; the rejecting nodes are 3, 1 and 4 at seed 35.

interpretations.rationale: The decoded operands name the two changes that make up the committed history: a joint-enter change removing node 4 (which changes no voter set, since node 4 is not a member) followed by a joint-enter change adding node 4, with only a normal entry between them and no leave-joint entry, applied in order by nodes 3, 1 and 4 (indices 18-20) and rejected at the second change with 'config is already joint'. The account of why the required leave is missing is now specific and source-grounded: appliedTo proposes the zero-change leave only when the node applying the joint change is the leader, so a joint change whose proposer is displaced before it applies its own change leaves the cluster joint with nobody having proposed the leave; the next leader then sees a non-joint tracker and a pendingConfIndex that predates the committed change, which is exactly the state the deterministic case at index 16 shows the guard admitting (pending_conf_index=0, applied=0, committed=2, joint_now=false, second proposal appended as EntryConfChangeV2). Index 21 keeps the counters and violations=0. The asserted availability defect therefore stands with three kinds of support: the guard admission under stale leader-local state (index 16), the actual changes in the committed history (indices 18-20), and the in-order application that reaches the rejection. Scope and counterweights are unchanged: the finding is about the unmitigated consequence under default validation rather than about the existence of a documented best-effort check, the rejecting nodes are never the leader, storage faults and other configuration sizes were not exercised, and the reachability of the leader-local state via a real election is still source-argued rather than produced end to end in a receipt.
counterevidence: The receipt shows which changes are in the log but not which node proposed each entry nor whether that proposer was displaced before applying it, so the reason no leave was appended remains an inference from the appliedTo condition plus the decoded changes.
The rejected history is one seed and one log position; violations=0 shows the four checked invariants were unaffected, so the claim remains about availability rather than about safety.

Config documents the propose-time checks as best-effort with false negatives, which explains why this path exists; what the receipts add is that the consequence is a panic the applying node cannot avoid while following its duty.
limitations: The leader-local state in the deterministic case is supplied rather than produced by a leadership change, so the election-to-stale-state path is still argued from source.
Only the first three rejections emit operands, and the decoded range is capped at eight entries, so longer histories would be truncated in this receipt.
The harness recovers the panic, so the receipt shows the rejection rather than a node ceasing to function; storage faults, other cluster sizes and a rejecting leader remain outside the event set.

knowledge.assertion: the propose-time guard consults the leader's own applied configuration, and that leader-local bound is what fails here
